_comment: The op catalog: one source of truth for what an implant can be asked to do.
server/ops.js reads this at startup. It is the catalog clients offer and the
contract the server validates against. The agent keeps its own table of what
it actually implements and advertises those names during the handshake, so a
new op on the agent shows up without touching the server, and an op the
server offers that the agent lacks is refused at request time with a real
error rather than the silent catch-all ignore.
`type` is the wire verb and is what the agent dispatches on. It is the join
key between this catalog and the C table, which is why the two have to agree:
server/test/ops.test.js runs the REAL agent and fails if the advertised set
and the executable set here ever drift apart.
cap is the capability name. A viewer must hold the cap to originate the op.
It is checked twice, independently: the server refuses to relay, and the
agent re-checks on arrival. A compromised control plane still cannot talk an
implant into running something its operator was never granted.
`alsoReply` marks the one legitimate case of a wire type appearing in both
the request and the reply direction: `term-end` is a viewer's 'close this
session' and, from the other side, the implant's 'closed'. The dispatcher
resolves this by origin, not by type - an implant socket is checked against
IMPLANT_ROUTABLE first - so the overlap is unambiguous. Declaring it keeps
the loader's uniqueness check meaningful instead of having to be switched
off, which is what an undocumented exception always turns into.

capabilities.exec: run a command line and read its output
capabilities.control: liveness control - tell a peer to go quiet
capabilities.update: replace the agent binary on a peer

ops.name: exec
ops.desc: Run a command line; returns stdout, stderr and the exit code

ops.name: shell.open
ops.desc: Open an interactive pseudo-terminal on the peer

ops.name: shell.input
ops.desc: Send keystrokes to an open shell session

ops.name: cancel
ops.desc: Terminate the command currently running on the peer; rc=0 if there was one, rc=1 if the peer was idle. Terminal sessions are not affected - use shell.close

ops.name: sleep
ops.desc: Tell the peer to drop the link and stay off the network for a while

ops.name: update
ops.desc: Push a new agent binary; the peer verifies the digest and installs. With restart=1 it relaunches now; default restart=0 applies the new image at the next agent start

implantOriginated.desc: output and exit code from an exec
whether there was anything running to cancel
the shell exited on its own
the session was closed by request
